alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic dysregulation
alerts.message: Guidelines list hyperglycemia as a DTG adverse effect and require pre-DTG glycaemia risk screening. Patient gained 17 kg in 18 months on TLD (65→82 kg, BMI 25.6→32.4), with new pre-diabetes (HbA1c 6.1%, fasting glucose 118), dyslipidaemia (LDL 148, triglycerides 212), acanthosis nigricans, rising BP (118/74→138/88), and fatigue. She has two baseline risk factors: family history of diabetes and rapid weight gain. Guidelines state clients with ≥2 hyperglycaemia risk factors should not be transitioned to DTG. Non-drug contributors include family history and obesity itself, but the temporal relationship to TLD strongly supports drug attribution.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for diabetes with OGTT; consider switching DTG to EFV400 or ATV/r per guidelines given ≥2 hyperglycaemia risk factors; address weight and metabolic risk with diet and exercise counselling.

alerts.title: Missing DTG glycaemia monitoring per guidelines
alerts.message: Guidelines require fasting or random blood glucose monitoring every 3 months for 6 months when initiating DTG in clients with ≥2 hyperglycaemia risk factors. This patient had pre-existing risk factors (family history of diabetes, baseline fasting glucose 92 mg/dL) at TLD switch 18 months ago, but no evidence of scheduled glucose monitoring during that period. Her current HbA1c 6.1% and fasting glucose 118 mg/dL confirm progression to pre-diabetes that may have been detected earlier with guideline-directed monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform fasting glucose or HbA1c every 3–6 months; repeat lipid panel; document ongoing metabolic surveillance in care plan.

alerts.title: No clinician plan for metabolic findings
alerts.message: Guidelines list DTG hyperglycaemia as a major toxicity requiring management. The clinician documented no assessment or plan despite the patient presenting with multiple DTG-associated metabolic abnormalities: significant weight gain, pre-diabetes range HbA1c, dyslipidaemia, and acanthosis nigricans. No medicine changes, orders, or referrals were recorded. The plan field is entirely blank, leaving these clinically significant findings unaddressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment of DTG metabolic toxicity; initiate lifestyle counselling; consider regimen review or referral for diabetes prevention; schedule follow-up.
